title: Claude Fable 5.1 builds the ops review in Slack
format_note: A scripted Slack thread plays as a tale: a boss asks for a deck, Claude reads the files and delivers, then a two-line tagline and logo.
one_thing: Claude does a rushed ops-review deck inside Slack and the human still makes the one real call; 'You still run the show.'

transcript.voice_style: No speech. Whisper returned only repeated 'Music' lines, so the story is carried by on-screen Slack messages and status labels.
transcript.script_shape: Message from a boss, a title, the team's ask, Claude's silent work shown as status labels, a human decision, the deck delivered, a tagline, a logo.

structure.frame0: f0001.jpg: beige desktop with blue folders ('Q3 Materials', 'Past Reviews'), a faded Slack toast from Fabian fading in and a cursor. Subject present, not black.
structure.first_3s: Fabian's toast 'Hey Vickie - hate to do this, but exec review moved to tomorrow.' goes sharp at 2 s over a blurred desktop; second line 'Any chance you can have the deck by 8AM?' at 3.7 s.

beats.what: Desktop with a Slack toast from Fabian: exec review moved to tomorrow, deck by 8AM.
Cut to title 'Let Claude handle more' fading in word by word on a plain beige ground.
Vickie types her reply in a Slack composer, @-mentions Claude and attaches last month's deck.
Teammates drop files (CSV, PNG); Claude reacts with a thumbs-up or eyes emoji on each.
Streak transition into a gridded canvas: file messages scatter and drift while a red line runs down the centre.
Thirteen cuts: circular iris opens on a spreadsheet and a log file, labels 'Analyzing data...' and 'Understanding incidents...'.
One long move along the red line past file cards marked read/scanned, labels 'Channel analysis complete', 'Starting to build the deck...'.
'ISSUE DETECTED' conflicting Week 2 spend; Claude pings Vickie, who answers 'Split the spend 40-60'; files merge into one.
'August ops review.pptx' card, then the #august-ops-review message 'Done' with confetti reactions.
Whip-pan to #leadership-team: Vickie shares the deck, replies of praise scroll up.
Tagline: 'Fable 5.1 runs bigger projects. You still run the show.'
Starburst appears; 'Claude' wordmark builds letter by letter over silence.

hero_moment.what: The finished deck lands in #august-ops-review and three emoji reactions (6, 7, 4) pop with confetti.

ending.cta_text: Fable 5.1 runs bigger projects. You still run the show.
ending.what: Two-line serif tagline held about 3.7 s, then a starburst and 'Claude' wordmark, then silence to the end.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Only 6 of 19 cuts fall outside one 4.2 s burst (13 cuts at 37.6-41.8 s). The longest shot is 29.3 s (34% of runtime), a continuous move; the rest is slow UI state changes.

look.ground: Warm off-white beige for title and tagline cards; white Slack panels; a grid-paper beige texture for the work section.
look.accent_use: One coral-red hand-drawn line runs through the work section (18-71 s); the coral starburst opens status labels and the logo. Nothing else is saturated.

look.depth: Soft shadows under Slack cards, defocus blur on the desktop at 2-6 s, a circular iris vignette at 37.6-41.8 s, and rotated cards at 52 s.

product_ui.notes: Messages and file names are large and readable (f0007, f0035). Card sub-labels ('read · variables logged') and the Slack panel at 66-70 s are small, about 10-14 px high at 720p. Table and log text in the iris is legible only through the crops.

motion.eases: Soft ease-out on entrances, with blur cross-fades and motion-blur streaks on the whip-pans. Exact curves not measured.

on_screen_lines.text: Hey Vickie - hate to do this, but exec review moved to tomorrow.
Any chance you can have the deck by 8AM?
@here leadership pulled the ops review up to tomorrow at 9 am ... need a deck from everything posted since last month's review ASAP.
ISSUE DETECTED: Conflicting totals for Week 2 spend! Flagging to the team.
Nearly done, but need your eyes on one issue ASAP. Week 2 data conflicts across two vendors.
Good catch! We switched to a new agency! Take the second report. Split the spend 40-60.
Done — duplicate removed and the deck is attached. Summary for the team leads is drafted, ready when you are.
Fable 5.1 runs bigger projects. You still run the show.

good.observation: The problem is shown as a real-looking Slack toast from a named person, not a caption, and it is readable at once.
The title and tagline cards use a quiet serif on plain beige, and each is held long enough: 2.1 s for 4 words, 3.7 s for 9 words.
A single coral line draws the eye through 29 s of drifting file cards and gives the long section a spine.
Status labels in coral italic ('Analyzing data...', 'ISSUE DETECTED') narrate the agent's work with no voiceover.
A human decision ('Split the spend 40-60') sits in the middle of the work, and the tagline pays it off.
Calm ending: tagline, a wordmark built letter by letter, then 1.8 s of silence.

weak.observation: Loudness is -19.3 LUFS with a true peak of -0.2 dBTP, quiet for social and above the -1 dBTP limit.
The agent's step cards use text about 10-14 px high at 720p (1.4-1.9% of frame height), below a phone-readable size.
Cuts are not locked to the music (0.158 vs chance 0.061), so the 13-cut burst reads as editing rather than rhythm.
The 'Done' message runs 35 words in a small panel and the 70-71 s frames are too brief to read.

rule_candidates.rule: End on a two-line tagline held at least 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word (9 words = 3.2 s), then the wordmark, then a silent tail of about 1.8 s.
Put the burst near mid-film: 13 cuts in 4.2 s at 46% of runtime, then follow it with a long calm shot (29.3 s) so the burst reads as an event.
A film may break the 1.8-3.5 s cut rate when one continuous camera move carries a third of the runtime and a visible line leads the eye.
rule_candidates.evidence: longest shot 29.33 s, 34.3% of runtime; mean shot 4.28 s

rule_candidates.rule: Open on the problem as a named person's message inside the product UI at the 2-4 s mark, with the desktop behind it, instead of a caption.
Use one thin accent line, hand-drawn in the brand colour, as the visual spine across a long section; keep every other mark neutral.

rule_candidates.rule: Hide the transition in the action: a screen whip-pan streak when the message moves to another channel (73.4 s) and an iris when the agent starts reading (38 s).
With no voiceover, carry the agent's progress in short status labels beside the cards ('Analyzing data...', 'Channel analysis complete') rather than only on card sub-text.
An owner-approved film can sit at -19.3 LUFS with a true peak of -0.2 dBTP; do not treat the -14 LUFS social master as a quality bar.
